siteTagline: In-depth loyalty-program hotel reviews across Southeast Asia
heroHeadline: Find your next *elite* stay across Southeast Asia

theme._note: Editorial-magazine palette (cream/ink, single deep-gold accent) approved 2026-08-03, replacing the original warm gold-on-charcoal/boxed-card look. Hairlines (divider/border, now unified to one value) replace bordered card boxes; panelA/panelB are the two alternating duotone placeholder-photo backgrounds used by EntityCard. Gold itself has no dark-mode-specific slot in the engine's token shape, so dark-mode components deliberately reuse primaryHover/primaryHover-dark as 'gold, tuned readable for that theme' rather than a literal hover state -- see Header/Footer/EntityCard/HubCard for that reuse.

_googleAnalyticsId_note: Set to the GA4 Measurement ID (G-XXXXXXXXXX) from the elitestay.travel GA4 property. BaseLayout injects gtag.js on every page when this is non-empty; empty string = analytics off.
_googleSiteVerification_note: Set to the token (the content="..." value) from Google Search Console's 'HTML tag' verification method. BaseLayout renders the <meta name=google-site-verification> tag when non-empty. Not needed if you verify via DNS or the linked GA4 property instead.

sourceConfig._research_note: Hotels are evergreen (no lapsing) and the value here is review synthesis, not discovery -- researchPerRunLimit is set higher relative to entity count than races', and researchIntervalDays shorter, because sentiment/first-hand commentary IS the product for this vertical, not a supporting layer.
sourceConfig.discoveryConstraints: Only include hotels currently enrolled in Marriott Bonvoy (any Bonvoy-participating brand: Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, W Hotels, JW Marriott, Marriott Hotels, Westin, Sheraton, Le Meridien, Renaissance, Autograph Collection, Courtyard, Four Points, etc.) located in one of the tracked cities. Do not include non-Bonvoy independent hotels, vacation rentals/serviced apartments, or hostels. If a source page mixes Bonvoy and non-Bonvoy properties, extract only the Bonvoy-enrolled ones.
sourceConfig._trustedAggregators_note: marriott.com's own destination/search pages are heavily client-rendered (same failure mode as World Athletics' calendar in the races instance -- a plain fetch returns navigation chrome and zero hotels), so discover-entities.js will need a text-rendering fetch strategy or a static per-city seed list rather than relying on these URLs directly. Kept here as the authoritative reference for manual research and for whichever fetch strategy discover-entities.js ends up using.

notes: Vertical instance config for 'hotels' (elitestay.travel -- renamed from StayElite/stayelite.travel on 2026-08-03 at the site owner's request; the repo folder/internal references still say 'stayelite' but that's cosmetic and doesn't affect the live site, which is fully config-driven off this file). Launch scope: Marriott Bonvoy ONLY for now, across 6 Southeast Asian cities spanning 5 countries (Singapore, Bangkok, Phuket, Kuala Lumpur, Bali, Ho Chi Minh City -- Jakarta was dropped from scope and replaced with Ho Chi Minh City on 2026-08-03, at the site owner's request, to broaden country coverage). Architecture is chain-agnostic by construction (same core-facts-registry pattern as every other vertical) -- adding World of Hyatt, Hilton Honors, or IHG One Rewards later means one new data/categories/*.json file plus real researched entities, never a template or route change. Because more loyalty programs are an explicit near-term roadmap item (not a hypothetical), user-facing copy (hero headline/subtext, region hub descriptions, kicker labels) is deliberately written as program-agnostic ('loyalty-program hotels', not 'Marriott Bonvoy hotels') even while Bonvoy is the only program actually live -- only the Marriott Bonvoy category page itself (data/categories/marriott-bonvoy.json) and each hotel's own core_facts should name the program explicitly, since those are correctly scoped to describe that one program. URL structure deliberately stays flat (/hotels/<slug>/, /categories/<slug>/, /regions/<slug>/) rather than nested /[program]/[city]/[slug] -- this is a brand-new domain with no indexed URLs to protect, and the flat model already gets 'add a chain without rebuilding' for free, matching how runsea.run works. The weekly refresh pipeline auto-commits directly to main when validation passes (an intentional deviation from the races instance's PR-only gate, at the site owner's request) -- see refresh workflow comments for the validation conditions that must pass before that happens.
